title: How to add a background image in Keynote on Mac: step by step for Keynote 15.4
metaTitle: How to Add a Background Image in Keynote on Mac (2026)
description: How to add a background image in Keynote on Mac: select the slide, choose Image Fill, insert your photo and pick a fill mode in Keynote 15.4.
targetKeyword: how to add a background image in keynote on mac
intro: To add a background image in Keynote on Mac, select the slide, click an empty spot on it, and open the Format sidebar. Then click Standard under Background, choose Image Fill, click Replace, and pick your photo from Content Hub or a file on your Mac.
tldr: Click an empty spot on the slide, not an object on it, then open the Format sidebar.
Under Background, click Standard, choose Image Fill from the pop-up, then click Replace.
Double-click your image, then pick a fill mode such as Scale to Fill or Scale to Fit.
Changing a layout's background changes every slide that uses that layout.
Apple's Mac pages list no keyboard shortcut for this task, so the steps use the mouse.

blocks.text: Check your Keynote version first

Start with the version, because menu names and sidebar layout can shift between releases. Apple's What's new page lists Keynote 15.4 as the latest Mac version. Keynote 15.4 for Mac requires macOS 26 or later. If your Mac runs an older system, the controls may look different.

The steps in this guide follow Apple's Mac background guide. That guide does not name a Keynote version, so read the menu names as current rather than guaranteed for every release. If your sidebar looks different, compare it with the What's new page before you assume the steps are wrong.
Apple's pages list no keyboard shortcut for this task. You work with the mouse, the Format sidebar and a file picker. That is slower than a shortcut, but it is the documented route.
Free Keynote or Apple Creator Studio

Apple still offers a free version of Keynote. Without a subscription, Keynote stays usable, but without the intelligence features. Creator Studio costs $12.99 per month or $129 per year in the US, according to Apple's January 2026 newsroom release. The Mac background guide does not mark Image Fill as a subscriber feature, but Apple does not say that outright, so check the Format sidebar on your own copy.
Pick the photo before you open Keynote

Choose the image before you start. A photo with a calm area works better behind text. Busy pictures compete with titles and bullet points. Look for open sky, a plain wall or a soft blur where the words will sit.
Use an image you have the right to use. Keynote's Content Hub is one source, and your own photos are another. Files from the web can carry license terms that limit how a public deck uses them.
Pick the right object before you click

This is the step that trips up most people. A slide can hold text boxes, shapes, images and tables. Each one has its own formatting. If you click an object, the Format sidebar changes that object, not the slide.
Click an empty spot on the slide before you look for Background. The sidebar should then show slide-level controls. If you see text or shape options instead, click a blank spot again.

Covered objects cause a quieter version of the same problem. Tables, charts and text boxes without their own fill show the slide's background color, according to Apple's iCloud guide. A table with a solid fill can hide the image you just added. If the image seems missing, check for a filled object sitting over the slide.
Choose the right fill mode

Choose Image Fill for a photo that covers the slide. Apple's Mac steps offer Advanced Image Fill for a tinted image. Once the image is in, the pop-up menu above Replace sets how the picture sits on the slide.

blocks.text: For a title slide, start with Scale to Fill. Switch to Scale to Fit if the important part of the photo sits near an edge. Each change shows on the slide right away, so compare two or three options before you choose.
A worked example: a title slide for a client talk

Say you need a title slide for a client talk. You have a photo of a harbor at dusk, with open water on the left. Click the empty slide area, open the Format sidebar, then choose Standard and Image Fill.

Click Replace, choose the harbor photo from your Mac, and double-click it. Set the fill mode to Scale to Fill. The water on the left stays clear, so the title can sit there in white. Play the slide full screen and check whether the title is still easy to read.
Use one background across many slides

If every slide in a section needs the same image, do not repeat the work on each slide. Apple says that changing a layout's background applies it to every slide that uses the layout. Edit the layout's master slide instead. The full process is in our [guide to editing the master slide](/how-to/edit-the-master-slide-in-keynote).
Be careful with scope. A change to one slide affects only that slide. A layout change can reach slides you have already styled, so review the deck after you edit a layout.
Background image or background color

A background image sits behind everything on the slide, the same way a background color does. A plain color is easier to match with a template, and it avoids questions about cropping. Choose an image when the photo should carry the slide.
Choose a color when the text, charts or diagrams should carry it. The same Background pop-up lets you switch the fill type, so you can test both on one slide before you commit.
Mac and iCloud steps differ

If you use Keynote for iCloud in a browser, the path is shorter. Apple's iCloud guide, written for version 14.1, says to select the slide, make sure the Background checkbox in the Format sidebar is selected, choose Image Fill, click Choose, and double-click an image.

The iCloud guide lists .jpg, .png and .gif files. It describes no Stretch, Tile or Scale options. Do not assume the web app works the way the Mac app does. Test the fit in the browser before you present.
Fix a background that will not change

Three problems cause most failures. The first is the object selection mistake covered above. The second is a locked or grouped object. Apple's add-an-image guide says that if you cannot replace an image, it may be locked or grouped. Remove the lock or ungroup the object, then try again.

The third is a background that vanishes. An Apple Community thread describes Keynote 12.1 on macOS 12.3, where background images disappeared after a few minutes of editing and left a question-mark icon. Updating Keynote did not fix it, and Apple community staff suggested a macOS update. The thread shows no confirmed fix, so save a copy of the deck before you change system software.
That thread is from 2022, so it may not match your version. Treat it as a warning sign, not a diagnosis.

items: Click a blank spot on the slide and confirm Background shows in the Format sidebar.
Check for a locked or grouped object sitting over the slide.
Look for a filled table, chart or text box covering the background.
Update macOS and Keynote, then reopen a saved copy of the deck.

blocks.text: Why slide work time is worth protecting

A background is a small change, but slide work adds up. A Venngage survey, cited by Outbrain, found that 47% of respondents said building their slide deck took more than 8 hours. The article does not state the sample size, so treat the figure as rough.

A GfK survey for Made in Office, reported by Imagine Layout, found that office workers spend about 20 hours a month in PowerPoint. Roughly 8 of those hours go to formatting. The Imagine Layout article does not give the survey year, and the original report was not checked here.
Mistakes people make

items: Clicking an object, then wondering why the slide background did not change.
Choosing Stretch for a photo of people, which can distort faces and bodies.
Changing a layout background when you only meant to change one slide.
Forgetting that a filled table or text box covers the image behind it.
Using a very large file, which can make the deck slow to edit.

blocks.text: Most of these come from working too fast. Slow down at the object selection step, and most of the rest goes away.
What to do next

Once the background is set, check the text on top. Then decide whether the slide needs a transition or an animation. The [transition guide](/how-to/add-a-transition-in-keynote) and the [object animation guide](/how-to/animate-an-object-in-keynote) cover those steps. If you reuse one look across decks, [importing a theme](/how-to/import-a-theme-in-keynote) saves setup time.

faq.question: Can I add a background image to every slide at once?
faq.answer: Yes, if the slides share a layout. Apple says a background change on a layout applies to every slide that uses that layout. To change one slide only, edit that slide and leave the layout alone.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut for this task?
faq.answer: Apple's Mac pages for this task list no keyboard shortcut. The steps use the mouse, the Format sidebar and the file picker. Other Keynote tasks may have shortcuts, but none is documented for this one.

faq.question: Which image file types work?
faq.answer: Apple's iCloud guide lists .jpg, .png and .gif. Its Mac steps do not list file types. Use .jpg or .png, and check the result on the Mac before you present.

faq.question: Why did my image end up in the wrong place on the slide?
faq.answer: Check the fill mode first. Original Size keeps the picture at its own size, and Tile repeats it. Switch to Scale to Fill or Scale to Fit, then compare the results.

faq.question: Do I need Apple Creator Studio to add a background image?
faq.answer: No subscription is needed to use Keynote. Apple says Keynote stays usable without a subscription, though without the intelligence features. Creator Studio costs $12.99 per month or $129 per year in the US.

faq.question: Why does my background disappear after I edit the slide?
faq.answer: A 2022 Apple Community thread describes that problem in Keynote 12.1 on macOS 12.3. The thread reports no confirmed fix. Update macOS and Keynote, then check a saved copy of the deck.

faq.question: Does Keynote for iCloud work the same way as the Mac app?
faq.answer: Not exactly. The iCloud guide uses the Format sidebar, a Background checkbox, Image Fill and Choose. It lists no Stretch, Tile or Scale options, so test the fit in the browser.

task: Add a background image to a slide in Keynote on Mac
appliesTo: Keynote 15.4 for Mac on macOS 26 or later. Older versions may differ.
requirements: A Mac running macOS 26 or later for Keynote 15.4
Keynote installed, free or with Apple Creator Studio
An image file on your Mac, or access to Content Hub
A slide where you can click an empty area

steps.name: Open the slide
steps.text: In the slide navigator on the left, click the thumbnail of the slide you want to change. The slide opens in the main canvas. Work on one slide at a time, so the change stays where you want it.
steps.tip: A background on one slide does not change the others unless you edit the layout.

steps.name: Click an empty area of the slide
steps.text: Click a blank spot on the slide where no text, picture or shape sits. Clicking an object selects it, and the Format sidebar then formats that object instead of the slide.
steps.tip: If the sidebar shows text or shape options, click a blank spot again.

steps.name: Open the Format sidebar
steps.text: Click the Format button in the toolbar. It looks like a paintbrush. The sidebar opens with controls for the current selection, which is now the slide.
steps.tip: A crowded toolbar can hide labels, so look for the paintbrush icon.

steps.name: Click Standard under Background
steps.text: Scroll to the Background controls in the Format sidebar. Click Standard. This keeps the slide in its basic fill until you pick an image.

steps.name: Choose Image Fill from the pop-up
steps.text: Open the background pop-up menu and choose Image Fill. For a tinted image, choose Advanced Image Fill instead. The controls below the pop-up change to image options.
steps.tip: Start with Image Fill if you want the photo exactly as it is.

steps.name: Click Replace
steps.text: Click Replace in the image options. Keynote then offers two sources, Search Content Hub and Choose File. Search Content Hub lets you look for an image without leaving Keynote. Choose File opens a picture stored on your Mac.

steps.name: Double-click your image
steps.text: Find the image in Content Hub or in the file window, then double-click it. Apple's Mac guide names double-clicking as the way to insert it. The image becomes the slide background.
steps.tip: If nothing changes, confirm the slide is still selected and try again.

steps.name: Pick a fill mode
steps.text: Open the pop-up menu above Replace and choose a fill mode. Scale to Fill covers the slide. Scale to Fit keeps the whole image visible. Tile repeats the image. Stretch can change the image's proportions.
steps.tip: Preview each mode before you commit, because changes show right away.

steps.name: Adjust the Scale slider if needed
steps.text: For Original Size and Tile, drag the Scale slider until the size looks right. Then move on to checking the slide.

steps.name: Check the slide in Play
steps.text: Click through the slides in the navigator, then play the slideshow full screen. Look at the text on top of the image, because a busy photo can make words hard to read.

steps.name: Optional: apply the image to a whole layout
steps.text: If every slide that uses a layout needs the same image, edit the layout's master slide rather than one slide. Apple says a background change on a layout applies to every slide using that layout.
steps.tip: Review the whole deck after a layout change, since it can reach slides you already styled.

troubleshooting.problem: The Background controls do not appear
troubleshooting.fix: An object is probably selected. Click a blank spot on the slide, then reopen the Format sidebar.

troubleshooting.problem: Replace does nothing or is unavailable
troubleshooting.fix: The image may be locked or grouped. Remove the lock or ungroup it, then try again, as Apple's add-an-image guide notes.

troubleshooting.problem: The background shows a question-mark icon
troubleshooting.fix: A 2022 Apple Community thread reports this on Keynote 12.1 and macOS 12.3 with no confirmed fix. Update macOS and Keynote, then reopen a saved copy.

troubleshooting.problem: A table or text box hides the background
troubleshooting.fix: Tables, charts and text boxes without their own fill show the slide background. Remove the fill from that object, or accept that it covers the image.
